status: PACKAGES — the code is built and committed, and all 54 rebuild unit tests pass. Three existing tests relied on today's ok answer without the semantic store, which K5 now refuses; I named them and did not change them (DEC-866). Two other points need a decision.
work_completed: Added `src/gov/rebuild/seed.py`. With a folder, or with none (then it reads `integration_store` from `governance/project/rebuild.yaml`), it follows a link once and checks that the folder holds `.gov-runtime/store.db`. It reads the base's `.gov-runtime/rebuild/stores.json` and compares it with this build: the code fingerprint, the schema, and the embedder the endpoint reports now. Any difference, or a missing record, gives `refused` with the reason named (`code fingerprint`, `schema`, `embedder model`, `no readable record`) and nothing is copied. A matching base is copied into a staging folder first: `store.db` through SQLite's backup, and the code-graph tool's home file by file (its SQLite files through backup) into the tree's own home. The copy is kept only if the base's record is unchanged afterwards and the copied store's semantic manifest matches the record. Any fault removes what was copied. `--no-embeddings --seed` copies no vectors and never asks the endpoint. A base that is the tree itself gives `none`. In `command.py`: `--seed [FOLDER]` (const = configured base); every rebuild deletes its own `stores.json` at the start (under the lock); a full rebuild writes it at the end from the semantic manifest (`code`, `embedder{model,revision}`, `schema`, `written_at`); the result has `seed` only when `--seed` was given. K5: a full rebuild whose semantic stage is unavailable or raises now raises `GovError("REBUILD_FAILED", …, {"store": "semantic", "reason": …})`. Code fingerprint chosen: `sha256:` over every file of the running `gov` package (path plus content, `__pycache__` skipped), plus the sha256 of the gitleaks binary on PATH, plus `sys.version` and `sqlite3.sqlite_version`. Why: this is the brief's simplest fail-closed choice, and I added the gitleaks binary because the pre-index filter decides which files become store entries, and lexical indexing does not re-judge files when the binary changes. Schema version: `sha256:` over `loader._TABLES`, `loader._FINGERPRINTS`, `lexical.SCHEMA` and `semantic.SCHEMA`, so it changes on its own when the tables change and never needs a manual bump.

discoveries: (1) `codeintel.index` deletes `.gov-runtime/codeintel` and builds it from scratch on every rebuild (W1-16), so the copied code-graph home (110M in W2-00-store) is thrown away at once and saves nothing today. (2) The secrets record (W2-107) is one machine-wide file (`~/.cache/gov-os/secrets-scan.sqlite`), not part of any tree. The base's verdicts are already the tree's, so nothing is copied for it; the seed's `copied` list names `.gov-runtime/store.db` and the code-graph home. (3) Because the fingerprint covers the whole `gov` package, any worktree whose ticket edits `src/gov/**` will always have its seed refused (`code fingerprint`) and rebuild cold. A fresh worktree at the integration head seeds. (4) The semantic stage needs the endpoint even when the path map embeds nothing (DEC-694), so such a project's full rebuild now fails when no endpoint answers. (5) Existing callers that relied on an ok answer without the semantic store. Run and red: tests/unit/secrets_check/test_w2_107_record.py:53 (stands the semantic stage in as unavailable, expects ok): `test_the_record_holds_every_kind_with_both_numbers` and `test_an_unchanged_second_rebuild_scans_only_the_planted_secret_again`. risks: Until the three test owners re-baseline, the suite has the reds listed in discoveries (5). On the shared runner on the GPU, vectors can depend on the prompt computed just before (DEC-773), so the lead's real-tree comparison of seeded and cold vectors may differ for reasons that have nothing to do with the seed. A base refreshed with `--no-embeddings` loses its `stores.json` and is refused until its next full rebuild (by design). I broke DEC-941 4a once: an empty here-document that ran as a no-op (`python3 - … <<'EOF'`). It was not refused, and I did not use it again.
lessons: All heavy-job slots were taken for more than 10 minutes, so `verify_lock.sh` timed out with no output; one test file per run works. `semantic._ask`, `semantic._ready` and `ollama.ensure_available` are the in-process stand-in points; setting `OLLAMA_HOST` to a closed port keeps the shared server out of reach. A throwaway repository for the real CLI needs a `.gitleaks.toml`.
proposed_decisions: P-1 (the tests that relied on an ok answer without the semantic store). Why now: they turn red as soon as this lands. Options: (a) their owners re-baseline them to the stricter behaviour: in W2-107's unit test, line 53 stands in `{"available": True}`; the W2-76 tests and W1-41's full cases expect `REBUILD_FAILED` with `store: semantic`, or use a stand-in endpoint; (b) exempt projects whose path map embeds nothing (DEC-694) from K5, which fixes W1-41 only. Impact: suite reds until done. Reversible, cost about 5 test lines. Recommend (a): high confidence for W2-107 and W2-76, medium for W1-41. P-2 (the code-graph copy is thrown away). Options: keep it (as built, about 110M copied per seed for nothing); drop it from the seed (−15 lines); or a later ticket that makes `codeintel.index` incremental. Reversible. Recommend dropping it now and filing the ticket if code-graph time matters; medium confidence. P-3 (the fingerprint's breadth). A narrower set of the modules that shape store entries would let tickets that edit `src/gov` seed, but missing one module would fail open. Recommend keeping it broad and revisiting only with the evidence K3 produces; medium-high confidence.
